narrative:
The model estimates a 47% chance that you will leave your job, which is high enough for the company to deny your promotion as a precaution.

The decision was driven mainly by three factors. First, your total years of experience across all jobs had the strongest influence and pulled the prediction toward staying. Most employees the model expects to stay also have 1-5 years of experience, so in this respect you look similar to loyal staff. Second, having received other job offers while at the company was the strongest factor pushing toward leaving. This signal of external opportunities raised the risk that you might depart. Third, working in the “other” sector also nudged the prediction upward, though less strongly; only 22% of employees predicted to stay work in this category, compared with higher shares in medical or education.

Taken together, the combination of solid external opportunities and a less common sector outweighed the stabilizing effect of your experience level, tipping the model just above the threshold for concern.

The organization should discuss your career goals openly and explore whether stronger internal opportunities or support could reduce the pull of outside offers. You may want to reflect on what would make staying feel more secure and fulfilling.
